import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I'm reading the lead's final report and the diagram manifest so I can put the canonical file together.

Now I'll review the assembled draft around the opening, the figures, and the restructured headings.

The draft keeps every line of the lead's content. The only differences are the heading renumbering, the in-document links, and the two figures. Next I'll check anchors with pandoc.

Registration succeeded. Now I'll finish the turn through the SASE final declaration.

I've published the lead's report as `202611/album_and_record_notes/album_and_record_notes.md` and registered it as a durable artifact (`research:202611/album_and_record_notes/album_and_record_notes.md`, ref `file:explicit:237eb17fc194094f3b134429`). The research repo commit has been declared and will be made when this turn ends.

**Inputs**
- **Source report:** there was exactly one lead report (`research:202611/album_and_record_notes/album_and_record_notes__final.md`), which I read through `sase artifact read`. I didn't modify it, the drafts, or the diagram manifest.
- **Diagram manifest:** its status was `ready`, it proposed 2 diagrams, and its `source` matched the lead's label. The `diagrams:` reference wouldn't resolve, so I read it through its `file:explicit:d0e2d52101b31df71aafa882` reference instead.

**Structure**
- **Opening:** the file opens with the title, a three-sentence research query, the infographic (it exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line`.
- **Section order:** Is this a good idea, What exists today, Requirement adjustments, Design, Migration and de-zorg, Glossary drafts and decision record, Risks, How the five reports were reconciled, Questions for you, Recommended solution, About this report, Sources.
- **Headings:** I removed the hand numbering. Headings that are link targets now contain only letters, digits, spaces and hyphens; any parenthetical or code I took out of them went into the section's first line. Two headings lost only their labels: "(verified)" and "(called out)". The first sentence of "What exists today" already says every number was rechecked.
- **Moved material:** the lead's byline and its restatement of the request now sit in "About this report".
- **Section references:** "§N" cross-references are now in-document links. The "see §5.4" inside the `eat.md` example code block is unchanged, because code blocks are copied byte-for-byte.

**Checks**
- **Coverage:** a line-by-line comparison found no dropped content. The only differences are headings, the added links, the figures, and the 12 horizontal rules between sections, which I dropped.
- **Tables:** all 10 tables and all 99 table rows are present.
- **Diagrams:** there are 3 Mermaid fences (the lead's 1 plus 2 accepted) and exactly 2 figure `<div>`s.
- **Anchors:** every `(#…)` link resolves when checked with pandoc in both its default and GitHub-flavored modes.
- **External links:** both URLs returned 200 (`https://obsidian.md/help/properties`, `https://obsidian.md/help/bases`). No link was unrepairable.

**Diagrams**
- **Accepted:**
  - `schema-failure` → `#figure-schema-failure`. It sits after the list in "A3 in detail", with its reference sentence in its own paragraph just above it.
  - `schema-cutover` → `#figure-schema-cutover`. It sits in "Phase 3 cutover", directly after the paragraph about the transition rule, and that paragraph ends with its reference sentence.
- **Omitted:** none.
